about: It's the Zork underground with its treasure hunt, reworked around the Flood Control Dam and the Frigid River. You open the sluice gates to drain the reservoir, pump up a boat, ride the river and pick up treasure along the banks. Then you have to get all of it home to the trophy case, and the house fights you on that. The trap door gets barred again every time you go down, and the only other way up is a studio chimney that takes you, your lamp and one more thing. So each treasure had to be carried up on its own trip.

done.why: I hit the 250-turn limit right after putting the gold coffin and the ivory torch in the case. I was holding the sceptre and walking toward the canyon to wave it at the rainbow for the pot of gold.

moments.note: The trap door slammed shut and someone barred it, just like the old game. I only found out later that it happens on every trip down, not just the first.
The troll went down in two blows. The haft of the sword knocked him out first.
The Round Room has passages that are blocked by cave-ins. That's new.
Weight limits kept stopping me, and the message kept saying 'the sword not least of it'. I ended up leaving the sword in the reservoir mud.
Turning the bolt with the wrench opened the sluice gates, and a few turns later the reservoir had drained to a stream with the jewel trunk lying in the mud. Very satisfying.
On the river the boat just sat at the dam landing while I waited. It didn't drift until after I typed 'go downstream', which the game said it didn't recognize.
I grabbed the buoy as the boat floated past and found the emerald inside.
The cave-in to the south of the Round Room had rubble 'sorted into neat heaps by size' and grit still trickling down. Someone has been working there. It made me curious.
The chimney only takes your lamp and one more thing, and the sack was too small to help. So it was one treasure per trip.
I opened the trap door from the living room and went down, and it was barred behind me again. Every trip home cost about ten moves.
A thief was leaning on the studio wall holding his bag. The gallery painting was gone soon after.
I sent several commands in a row and 'read paper' picked the paper up without asking, so the chimney refused me. That wasted about ten turns.
Praying at the altar took me straight up to the forest still carrying the heavy coffin. A lovely way around the chimney.

wished: I wanted to use the sceptre on the rainbow and get the pot of gold before I ran out of turns.
I wished I could take the trap door's bar off from the cellar side, or wedge the door open, so I didn't have to haul one item at a time up the chimney.
I wanted to clear the sorted rubble in the Round Room's south passage, or at least find out who sorted it.
I wanted to get the painting back from the thief.
I wished the boat drifted downstream when I said 'wait' or 'float', instead of needing a command it said it didn't recognize.

lines.line: The sluice gates open and water pours through the dam.
lines.why: This was the key that opened up the dam and river part of the game, and it worked the first time I tried it.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest. Behind the heaps the roof has come down all the way to the floor, and it has not finished coming down: grit is still trickling from it as you watch.
lines.why: It's the clearest sign that this cave is different from the one I knew. Someone is digging, and I never found out who.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: This one rule decided how I spent most of my turns.

lines.line: He does not speak, but it is clear from his aspect that the bag will be taken only over his dead body.
lines.why: The thief showing up made me nervous about everything I'd left lying in the studio.

lines.line: You notice, however, that the water level appears to be dropping at a rapid rate.
lines.why: It confirmed the dam had worked and told me to wait.

fun.why: Draining the dam, riding the river and grabbing the buoy all paid off nicely. Praying my way home with the coffin felt clever. The fun dropped during the long one-item chimney trips.

engagement.why: I always had a clear next goal, and the score kept going up: 35, then 75, then 100, and more after that. The long hauling stretches were where I cared least.

difficulty.why: Most of the puzzles made sense. The two hard things were the chimney limit combined with a trap door that re-bars every time, and the boat not drifting. Both cost turns rather than blocking me.

interestingness.why: The changes to the classic layout made me pay attention: the cave-ins with sorted rubble, the chimney rule and the trap door that keeps getting barred. They made getting treasure home into its own puzzle.

prose.why: The writing has the classic dry humor, and the new lines fit in well, especially the rubble and the chimney. Some rooms only showed their names when I came back, which is fine.
